# Memory observations

Record role, platform, compiler/version, build type and commands. Keep the
prediction, untouched observation and named repair separately.

| Current PC/instruction | Owned base and valid byte range | Actual address and width | Value before/after | Next PC and reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

For the pointer table draw four sixteen-byte records and four pointer slots.
Record the masked index, rotation, slot address, pointer stored in that slot,
selected record address and the field addresses. Separate address calculation
from the pointer load and the final field load. Use the pinned C offsets.

For the overlapping copy draw all sixteen original bytes and the source and
destination spans. Predict each byte read before its corresponding write.
Explain when a forward write destroys a later source byte. Record the actual
load/store PCs, offsets, remaining count and memory after each write.

Retain default/--changed observations, a separate boundary prediction, zero
length, both overlap directions, GCC/Clang Debug/Release checks and a rejected
copied regression. Preserve main.c, lab.h, model.c, tests.c and abi_checks.S.
Passing tests does not complete the address and memory trace.

.text
.globl abi_probe
.type abi_probe, @function
abi_probe:
    push rbp
    push rbx
    push r12
    push r13
    push r14
    push r15
    sub rsp, 24

    mov rsi, rdx

    mov r11, QWORD PTR [rsp + 8]

    mov r10, 0x13579bdf2468ace0
    cmp rbx, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x2468ace013579bdf
    cmp rbp, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x1122334455667788
    cmp r12, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done

    cmp r13, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(MemoryLayoutLab LANGUAGES C ASM)
if(NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux" OR NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(x86_64|amd64|AMD64)$")

endif()
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
add_executable(app main.c model.c routine.S)
add_executable(contracts tests.c model.c abi_checks.S routine.S)
foreach(target IN ITEMS app contracts)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic;-Wconversion;-Werror>")
endforeach()
enable_testing()
add_test(NAME memory_layout_contract COMMAND contracts)

.intel_syntax noprefix
.text
.globl lab_operation
.type lab_operation, @function
lab_operation:
    sub rsp, 96
    mov r8, rsp
    mov r10, rsi
    and r10d, 3
    xor ecx, ecx
lab_initialize:
    mov rax, rsi
    add rax, rcx
    mov QWORD PTR [r8], rax
    imul eax, ecx, 0x1111
    xor eax, esi
    mov WORD PTR [r8 + 8], ax
    mov BYTE PTR [r8 + 10], cl
    mov BYTE PTR [r8 + 11], 0xa5
    mov rax, rsi
    shr rax, 16
    imul r9d, ecx, 0x01010101
    xor eax, r9d
    mov DWORD PTR [r8 + 12], eax
    mov r9, rcx
    add r9, r10
    and r9d, 3
    shl r9, 4
    add r9, rsp
    mov QWORD PTR [rsp + rcx*8 + 64], r9
    add r8, 16
    inc ecx
    cmp ecx, 4
    jne lab_initialize
    mov rax, rdi
    and eax, 3
.globl lab_lookup
lab_lookup:
    # POINTER_LOOKUP: select the pointer slot for the masked index
    mov r8, QWORD PTR [rsp + 64] # incomplete pointer slot
.globl lab_selected
lab_selected:
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 0], rax
    movzx r9d, BYTE PTR [r8 + 10]
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 8], r9
    mov r9d, DWORD PTR [r8 + 12]
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 16], r9
    movzx r9d, WORD PTR [r8 + 8]
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 24], r9
    sub r8, rsp
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 32], r8
    add rsp, 96
.globl lab_return
lab_return:
    ret
.size lab_operation, .-lab_operation
.section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

# Pointer Table Lookup and Record Fields

## Exact owned-memory contract

`lab_operation(uint64_t initial, uint64_t incoming, LabResult *output)` receives
two unsigned values in RDI/RSI and an owned five-word output object in RDX.
The routine creates its own bounded scratch storage. No input integer is an
arbitrary pointer. All six callee-saved registers, RSP and the return address
must retain their entry values. This is a Linux x86-64 System V leaf function.

The scratch frame contains four `LabRecord` objects followed by four pointers.
Each record is sixteen bytes: counter at offset 0 (eight bytes), tag at 8 (two),
state at 10 (one), reserved at 11 (one) and weight at 12 (four). The C header
asserts this exact layout. Record i has counter incoming+i, tag the low sixteen
bits of incoming XOR i*1111 hexadecimal, state i, reserved a5 and weight the low
32 bits of (incoming>>16) XOR i*01010101 hexadecimal.

The pointer table is a rotated order of the records: slot i stores the address
of record `(i + (incoming & 3)) & 3`. Select slot `initial & 3`. Outputs are
that table index, the selected record's state/index, weight, tag and its byte
offset from the start of the record array. A slot advances by eight bytes; a
record advances by sixteen. Loading a pointer from a slot and loading a field
through that pointer are separate operations.

The starter always loads slot zero. Repair only POINTER_LOOKUP so the masked
index scales by eight in the table address. Preserve the table construction,
record contents, field widths and 96-byte frame. At lab_lookup predict the slot
address and stored pointer; at lab_selected inspect the selected record and
its tag/state/weight with their actual widths. Compare a nonzero table index.

The Unit 1 required decoder follows a flat packed byte format through source,
objects and loading. This optional Unit 7 task follows an actual pointer table
and a pinned C structure layout; it does not repeat that artifact trail.

In a disposable reference copy change `movzx r9d, WORD PTR [r8 + 8]` to
`movzx r9d, BYTE PTR [r8 + 8]`. The address remains valid but the tag loses its
upper byte. The default and unchanged contracts reject this width regression.

## Predict, build and explain

Default initial is `010203040506070a`, incoming `8123456789abcdef`. The correct five
hexadecimal outputs, in the declared order, are:

`0000000000000002 0000000000000001 00000000446688aa 000000000000dcfe 0000000000000010`

`--changed` uses zero for both inputs. This special case agrees even with the
named starter mistake and copied regression; it does not prove the general
contract. Predict another nonzero index or unequal overlapping span before
running it. The untouched starter builds but its default demo exits 78 and
unchanged contracts fail. Complete only POINTER_LOOKUP in `routine.S`.

Use ordinary-user Linux x86-64, GNU Intel assembly syntax, CMake 3.20+, GCC or
Clang, GDB and binutils. On macOS use an x86-64 Linux lab or VM; on Windows use
an x86-64 WSL distribution. The site IDE edits, saves and exports these sources.
Each role includes routine.S, main.c, lab.h, model.c, tests.c, abi_checks.S,
CMakeLists.txt and trace.md. Roles differ only in routine.S. Keep this README
one level above the selected role. From that role directory:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-Debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-Debug --verbose --parallel 1
./build-Debug/app
ctest --test-dir build-Debug --output-on-failure
./build-Debug/app --changed
cmake -S . -B build-Release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-Release --verbose --parallel 1
ctest --test-dir build-Release --output-on-failure
./build-Release/app --changed
objdump -d -M intel build-Debug/app
gdb ./build-Debug/app
```

Repeat with GCC in separate build directories. Unsupported arguments exit 64.
The independent C model uses C record/pointer expressions for the table task
and memmove for the overlap task. It never calls the assembly operation. The
unchanged explicit checks remain active in Release and cover 10,269 pairs:
sixteen boundary values crossed with themselves and 10,013 deterministic
additional pairs. The separate probe checks the six preserved registers and
stack restoration. Preserve the supplied C files and ABI probe.

In GDB use `set disassembly-flavor intel`, `break lab_operation` and `run`.
Save `set $entry_sp = $rsp`, `set $return_pc = *(unsigned long long*)$rsp`
and `set $output = $rdx`. Follow the task's labeled memory operations. Record
current instruction PCs, actual addresses, valid byte ranges, access widths
and before/after values. At lab_return check the original RSP and return word,
inspect all five output words through `$output`, then step RET to verify the
caller PC and `$rsp == $entry_sp + 8`. Use current addresses for each run.

Retain the untouched failure, named repair, actual memory trace, both compiler
and build modes, a boundary prediction and the rejected copied regression in
trace.md. Code tests do not complete that explanation.

References: [System V AMD64 ABI](https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI/-/blob/master/x86-64-ABI/low-level-sys-info.tex),
[memmove contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/memmove.3.html).

lab_operation:

    mov rax, 0x100f0e0d0c0b0a09

    mov r10d, 16

    cmp rcx, r10

    mov r10d, 16
    sub r10, r9
    cmp rcx, r10
    cmova rcx, r10
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 16], rcx
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 24], r8
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 32], r9
.globl lab_ready
lab_ready:
    test rcx, rcx
    jz lab_copy_done
.globl lab_direction
lab_direction:
    cmp r9, r8
    # COPY_DIRECTION: a higher destination uses the backward loop
    ja lab_backward
lab_forward:
.globl lab_forward_load
lab_forward_load:
    mov al, BYTE PTR [rsp + r8]
.globl lab_forward_store
lab_forward_store:
    mov BYTE PTR [rsp + r9], al
    inc r8
    inc r9
    dec rcx
    jnz lab_forward_load
    jmp lab_copy_done
lab_backward:
    add r8, rcx
    dec r8
    add r9, rcx
    dec r9
.globl lab_backward_load
lab_backward_load:
    mov al, BYTE PTR [rsp + r8]
.globl lab_backward_store
lab_backward_store:
    mov BYTE PTR [rsp + r9], al
    dec r8
    dec r9
    dec rcx
    jnz lab_backward_load
.globl lab_copy_done
lab_copy_done:
    mov rax, QWORD PTR [rsp]
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx], rax
    mov rax, QWORD PTR [rsp + 8]
    mov QWORD PTR [rdx + 8], rax

# Bounded Overlap Copy Direction

## Exact owned-memory contract

`lab_operation(uint64_t initial, uint64_t incoming, LabResult *output)` receives
two unsigned values in RDI/RSI and an owned five-word output object in RDX.
The routine creates its own bounded scratch storage. No input integer is an
arbitrary pointer. All six callee-saved registers, RSP and the return address
must retain their entry values. This is a Linux x86-64 System V leaf function.

The sixteen scratch bytes initially contain 01 through 10 hexadecimal.
Source offset is `initial & 7`, destination offset is `incoming & 7`, and the
requested length is `(initial >> 3) & 15`. Clamp length to both `16-source`
and `16-destination` before copying. The required result is the same as first
preserving the entire original source span and then writing its bytes at the
destination. Bytes outside the destination span remain unchanged.

Outputs are the final first and second eight-byte little-endian words, actual
copied count, original source offset and original destination offset. Zero
length performs no byte read or write. A higher destination uses the backward
loop; other destinations use the forward loop. Backward copying is also valid
for disjoint spans. The routine uses ordinary byte loads/stores, so it never
changes the processor direction flag.

The starter chooses the opposite direction. Repair only COPY_DIRECTION to
select backward copying when destination is higher. Keep the bounds, zero
guard, loops and output stores unchanged. For the default src=1, dst=3,
count=6, forward copying overwrites source bytes before later reads. Predict
that corruption, then compare the repaired trace with preserving the original
source span. At each load/store label record offsets and owned memory.

The required Unit 7 string routine requires non-overlapping spans and counts a
zero-terminated source. This optional challenge copies a clamped byte count
with overlap; it has no string terminator contract.

In a disposable reference copy replace `ja lab_backward` with `jmp lab_forward`.
The unchanged contracts and overlapping default reject always-forward copying.

## Predict, build and explain

Default initial is `0000000000000031`, incoming `0000000000000003`. The correct five
hexadecimal outputs, in the declared order, are:

`0605040302030201 100f0e0d0c0b0a07 0000000000000006 0000000000000001 0000000000000003`

`--changed` uses zero for both inputs. This special case agrees even with the
named starter mistake and copied regression; it does not prove the general
contract. Predict another nonzero index or unequal overlapping span before
running it. The untouched starter builds but its default demo exits 78 and
unchanged contracts fail. Complete only COPY_DIRECTION in `routine.S`.

Use ordinary-user Linux x86-64, GNU Intel assembly syntax, CMake 3.20+, GCC or
Clang, GDB and binutils. On macOS use an x86-64 Linux lab or VM; on Windows use
an x86-64 WSL distribution. The site IDE edits, saves and exports these sources.
Each role includes routine.S, main.c, lab.h, model.c, tests.c, abi_checks.S,
CMakeLists.txt and trace.md. Roles differ only in routine.S. Keep this README
one level above the selected role. From that role directory:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-Debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-Debug --verbose --parallel 1
./build-Debug/app
ctest --test-dir build-Debug --output-on-failure
./build-Debug/app --changed
cmake -S . -B build-Release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-Release --verbose --parallel 1
ctest --test-dir build-Release --output-on-failure
./build-Release/app --changed
objdump -d -M intel build-Debug/app
gdb ./build-Debug/app
```

Repeat with GCC in separate build directories. Unsupported arguments exit 64.
The independent C model uses C record/pointer expressions for the table task
and memmove for the overlap task. It never calls the assembly operation. The
unchanged explicit checks remain active in Release and cover 10,269 pairs:
sixteen boundary values crossed with themselves and 10,013 deterministic
additional pairs. The separate probe checks the six preserved registers and
stack restoration. Preserve the supplied C files and ABI probe.

In GDB use `set disassembly-flavor intel`, `break lab_operation` and `run`.
Save `set $entry_sp = $rsp`, `set $return_pc = *(unsigned long long*)$rsp`
and `set $output = $rdx`. Follow the task's labeled memory operations. Record
current instruction PCs, actual addresses, valid byte ranges, access widths
and before/after values. At lab_return check the original RSP and return word,
inspect all five output words through `$output`, then step RET to verify the
caller PC and `$rsp == $entry_sp + 8`. Use current addresses for each run.

Retain the untouched failure, named repair, actual memory trace, both compiler
and build modes, a boundary prediction and the rejected copied regression in
trace.md. Code tests do not complete that explanation.
